intent: Change one thing: widen the sensor array from ±0.04 to ±0.06 m and enlarge the footprint from 12 mm to 16 mm, so the line stays in view past the 0.06 m off-track limit. Keep the forward offset (y = 0.03), wheels, body and mass as in the baseline so the telemetry isolates the sensing change. Expected result: line_loss_events near 0, max_error below 0.06 m on more trials, and progress and completion improving on the oval and s-bend. Under consideration, not committed: a 7-sensor array at 0.02 m spacing if the Integrator finds a 5-sensor signal too coarse, and a shorter forward offset (y = 0.02) if the robot still reacts late on the slalom.
learning: The off-track limit is fixed at 0.06 m for every allowed body width, so the binding limit is sensor reach. Test whether the array span, not the controller, explains the one-line-loss-then-off-track pattern. If line_loss_events stays at 1 with the wider array, the cause is the controller's recovery, not the geometry.
rationale: Race evidence for the baseline (entityR2A, 60 trials): every run ended off_track, none finished, and each run had exactly one line-loss event. Max error sat at about 0.062 to 0.063 m on all three tracks, just above the off-track limit. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). With body_width at most 0.18 that limit is always 0.06 m, so body width cannot buy margin. The baseline sensors sit at x = ±0.04 with a 0.012 m footprint, so a sensor sees the tape only while the line centre is within about 0.0185 m of it. The line therefore drops out of view at roughly 0.0585 m of offset, just before the 0.06 m off-track limit. The sequence fits the data: the robot tracks well (rms_error about 0.023 to 0.026 m), then one bend pushes it past the edge of the array. Once the line is lost the robot cannot recover, so it leaves the track. The limiting factor is the array's lateral span, not the body or the forward offset. I am taking the Integrator's advice from iteration 0 only in spirit: there is no Integrator feedback yet, so the change comes from race data alone. I am widening the array to x = ±0.06 with 0.016 m footprints. A sensor at x = 0.06 then sees the tape for offsets up to about 0.0805 m, well past the 0.06 m limit, so the controller keeps a signal during the excursions that currently end runs. I keep the 0.03 m forward offset, wheel geometry, body and mass unchanged, so the race isolates the sensor-span change. Expected result: line_loss_events falls to 0 or near 0 on the development tracks, max_error stays under 0.06 more often, and progress rises on the oval and s-bend. The main risk is that wider spacing (0.03 m, larger than the 0.025 m tape) gives a flatter signal near centre, which may need a smaller kp from the Integrator.
